diagnostic_evidence.quote: The global minimum is zero in these cases, but the RK2 landscape reveals multiple distinct points that achieve this optimum.

issues.failure_explanation: Zero loss in the stated problem only requires p(xi)^m=e^{lambda hm}, not p(xi)=e^{lambda h}. Thus there are m temporal aliases even for Forward Euler, and Runge-Kutta polynomials add further inverse branches. For example, with m=2 and lambda h=i pi/2, both p(xi)=i and p(xi)=-i give zero loss, but their imaginary parts have opposite signs. The paper instead applies properties of one selected solution of p(xi)=e^{lambda h} to an unqualified global minimizer.

issues.failure_explanation: The fitted sequence only shows that one characteristic root has modulus one. Other roots may already lie outside the unit disk, placing the parameter outside the closure rather than on its boundary. Moreover, under the paper's strict definition |z|<1, Leap-Frog has no absolutely stable parameter because the product of its two root moduli is one; its asserted imaginary stability interval is therefore incompatible with that definition.

issues.overall_effect: The main connection between conservative LMM learning and the boundary of absolute stability, including the Leap-Frog discussion based on it, is unsupported.
issues.title: A unit characteristic root does not prove membership in the boundary of the LMM stability region
issues.why_classification: The one-line inference omits the defining all-roots condition and requires a new method-dependent root analysis; the present stability-region conclusions do not follow.

issues.failure_explanation: A product of modulus one implies that if one root is strictly inside then the other is outside, not that one is always outside. At lambda h=0 the roots of the displayed recurrence are 1 and -1, both on the unit circle; throughout the appropriate imaginary interval they can both have modulus one.
